label: accumulated i/a/g/o/j tokens, through the delimiter and first copy step
explanation: Weak, diffuse unit. It is most active at the <DEL> step (rate 17.7%, 3.5x lift, 32% of activation mass) and at original steps t=2-4, and much less in the copy phase after the first output. It never fires at t=0. Its rate goes up when the inputs so far include the tokens i, a, g, o, j: lift 2-3.9x by prev2_tok, 2.6x when first_tok is i. The top activations are short prefixes made of these tokens, e.g. a i a <DEL>. Best predicate: at least two of {i,a,g,o,j} seen so far and recall_idx<=1. It gets dev F1 0.33 with precision about 0.26 and mass recall 0.61. Many delimiter and early-original steps that have such prefixes stay inactive, and some activations have none of these tokens before them. So this is a tendency, not a clean rule. Magnitude is larger on the delimiter step and in higher quartiles (coverage of the top quartile is about 0.7). Mid/late copy steps and t=0 are almost always inactive.
